name: Soul Tether

relationships.label: Soul Tether is derived from the First Moon Ritual — it is a simplified, repeatable version of the anchoring technique Yssara revealed to the First Voice.
The Pale-Touched use Soul Tether to slow their transformation, stretching the time between stages by anchoring their soul each day — it does not stop the erosion, only delays it.
The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion considers Soul Tether cheating — delaying holy erosion is seen as resistance to Yssara's will, a sin of cowardice dressed as self-preservation.

description: Soul Tether is the most common moon-magic spell in Northern Velkaris — the first lesson every mage learns. It temporarily anchors the caster's soul to their body, slowing the erosion caused by moon fragment exposure. It does not stop erosion. It does not reverse damage. It buys time. Every mage in the region knows this spell. Every mage uses it daily. Every mage is still dying — just slower.
excerpt: The most common moon-magic spell — anchors the soul to delay erosion. Does not stop it. Every mage learns this first.
content:
Soul Tether is the first spell every mage in Northern Velkaris learns. It is not taught in a classroom — it is taught by a parent, an elder, a senior Tide-Weaver, a scar-faced veteran of the Remnants who grabs the student's hand, presses a moon fragment into it, and says: feel that? That's your soul leaking. Now hold it still.

The mechanics are simple. The caster visualizes their soul as a thread, one end tied to their body, the other fraying into the fragment's glow. The spell pulls the frayed end back and knots it — temporarily. The knot holds for a few hours, maybe a day for experienced casters. While it holds, the fragment's erosion slows to a crawl. The caster can handle fragments, cast other spells, work through the night without advancing to the next stage. When the knot loosens, the erosion resumes at its natural pace.

Soul Tether does not heal. This is the first disappointment every new caster faces. You cannot reclaim what you have already lost. You can only keep what remains. The Greyvasti elders teach the spell with a warning carved into the lesson: the tethered soul is still a leaking soul. You are only borrowing time, and the debt comes due all at once when the knot breaks.

The Pale Dominion has a complicated relationship with Soul Tether. The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion teaches that erosion is sacred, that every fragment of soul offered to Yssara is an act of worship. To delay erosion is to withhold worship. The Arch-Seers have not outlawed the spell — too many Dominion citizens rely on it — but they preach against it, classifying it as a sin of weakness rather than malice. The faithful who use Soul Tether are encouraged to offer additional soul-fragments in ritual to compensate for the delay. Most do. The cycle continues.

name: Moonblind

relationships.label: Moonblind is a standard combat spell used by the Oathbound Remnants — a quick flash of concentrated moon-light that buys time to close distance or retreat.
Moonblind is taught in the military doctrine of the Pale Dominion — Dominion soldiers are trained to cast it as a non-lethal disabling tool during arrests and interrogations.
Moonblind is entirely ineffective against Fracture Wyrms — they have no eyes, and the spell's light component has no effect on their sensory apparatus.

description: Moonblind is a weaponized moon-magic spell that floods the target's vision with raw lunar light, causing temporary or permanent blindness. It is a standard combat spell across Northern Velkaris — the Oathbound Remnants use it for quick disengagement, the Pale Dominion teaches it as a non-lethal tool, and every mage knows how to counter it. It causes minor soul erosion in the caster with each use.
excerpt: Weaponized moon-light — floods the target's vision, causing temporary or permanent blindness. Standard combat spell across Northern Velkaris.
content:
Moonblind is a crude spell, and its crudeness is the point. It does not require precision, finesse, or careful control. It requires a moon fragment, a line of sight, and the willingness to burn a small piece of your soul to blind someone else.

The caster channels fragment energy through their palm and releases it as a focused burst of silver-white light. The effect is immediate and overwhelming — the target's pupils contract to pinpricks, their vision floods with afterimages, and for several seconds they see nothing at all. An overcharged casting can burn the retina permanently, leaving the victim with two silver-white scars where their vision used to be.

The Oathbound Remnants favor Moonblind for quick disengagement. A Remnant pinned behind cover will fire a burst of Moonblind into the open, sprint across while the enemy blinks silver, and vanish into the mist before anyone's vision clears. They do not use it to kill. They use it to survive.

The Pale Dominion teaches Moonblind as a non-lethal tool. Dominion soldiers are trained to cast it at low intensity — just enough to disable, not enough to burn. It is used during arrests, crowd control, and interrogations where a corpse would be inconvenient. The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion approves of this restraint: blindness is a controlled erosion of sight, a measured offering.

name: Hollow Whisper

relationships.label: Hollow Whisper draws power from Mourne the Hollow King — it calls on his domain over the dead, borrowing his attention for sixty seconds to allow the caster to speak with a soul he has collected.
The Hollow Covenant uses Hollow Whisper as a deathbed ritual — the dying speak their final oath through the spell, ensuring Mourne hears and remembers their name.
The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion condemns Hollow Whisper as necromantic heresy — to speak with the dead is to interfere with Yssara's natural order of dissolution and forgetting.

description: Hollow Whisper is a spell that calls on Mourne the Hollow King, allowing the caster to speak with the recently dead for sixty seconds. The cost is severe — a memory, permanently erased from the caster's mind, taken by Mourne as payment. The Hollow Covenant considers it sacred, used in deathbed rituals so the dying can swear their final oath. The Pale Dominion condemns it as necromantic heresy, a violation of Yssara's natural order.
excerpt: Speak with the dead for sixty seconds by offering Mourne a memory in payment. Sacred to the Hollow Covenant. Heresy to the Pale Dominion.
content:
Hollow Whisper is not a spell you learn from a book. It is a spell you receive — passed from one caster to another in a moment of trust so absolute that both parties are willing to lose a memory for it. The teaching itself is evidence of the bond: the teacher casts the spell, speaks the secret into the student's ear, and the student loses sixty seconds of their life that they will never remember.

The spell requires a corpse. The body must be present — a name in the mist is not enough. The caster kneels beside the dead, places one hand on the chest where the heart used to be, and speaks the name of Mourne three times: once for the soul that left, once for the memory being offered, once for the sixty seconds to come. Mourne does not answer in words. The dead do. For exactly sixty seconds, the corpse speaks in its own voice, with its own mind, and the caster can ask anything.

The cost is taken immediately. The caster feels the memory vanish — a specific moment, a face, a place, a sensation, gone. They will not know what they lost until they try to remember it and find nothing. The memory does not fade. It is not suppressed. It is removed, as if it never existed, taken by Mourne into his collection.

The Hollow Covenant uses Hollow Whisper as a deathbed ritual. A Greyvasti who has minutes left to live will cast the spell on themselves, using their own death as the anchor, and speak their final oath through Mourne. The Covenant believes this ensures the oath is heard and remembered. The Pale Dominion has a different view. They classify Hollow Whisper as necromantic heresy — the first category in the Catalog of Prohibited Applications, the section the Tide-Weavers stole. The Dominion's position is that the dead belong to Yssara, not to Mourne, and any spell that treats death as a negotiation is an offense against the natural order.

name: Fragment Pulse

relationships.label: Fragment Pulse was invented by Tide-Weaver combat mages who needed a way to clear Fracture Wyrms from collapsed tunnels — it sacrifices the fragment for a single, devastating burst of energy.
Fragment Pulse's primary use is against Fracture Wyrms — the overpressure wave created by detonating a Grade 3 fragment in a confined tunnel is the only reliable way to kill or drive off a wyrm.
Fragment Pulse consumes a moon fragment as its fuel source — the spell channels all of the fragment's stored energy into a single burst, completely destroying the fragment in the process.

description: Fragment Pulse is a last-resort combat spell invented by the Tide-Weavers to clear Fracture Wyrms from excavation tunnels. It detonates a moon fragment's stored energy in a single, devastating burst — destroying the fragment completely and dealing massive damage in a contained radius. The soul erosion cost to the caster is severe, and the spell is only used when retreat is not an option.
excerpt: Detonates a moon fragment's stored energy in a single burst — destroys the fragment, massive damage, massive soul cost. Last resort.
content:
Fragment Pulse is the closest thing Northern Velkaris has to a controlled explosion of divine power, and it kills whoever uses it within a few years.

The spell was invented by Tide-Weaver combat mages who kept losing crews to Fracture Wyrms in collapsed tunnels. Standard weapons did nothing. Moonblind had no effect. The wyrms were too large, too deep, too indifferent to anything except the moon fragments they were eating — fragments that the Tide-Weavers needed to recover. The solution was obvious in retrospect: use the fragment itself as the weapon.

Fragment Pulse channels all of the fragment's stored energy — every lumen of moonlight, every resonance, every accumulated charge — into a single directional burst. The fragment shatters. The energy releases as a shockwave of silver light and concussive force that can collapse a tunnel, shatter stone, and liquify organic matter within twenty feet. A Grade 3 fragment, properly focused, can kill a juvenile Fracture Wyrm instantly. A Grade 4 can stagger an adult. Nothing larger has been tested, because nothing larger has survived the casting.

The cost to the caster is brutal. The spell channels the fragment's energy through the caster's body, and the soul erosion is immediate and severe. A single casting of Fragment Pulse advances the caster approximately one full stage of Pale-Touched transformation. Three castings, and the caster is beyond saving. The Tide-Weavers do not train specialists for this spell. They train volunteers — mages who know they are dying and choose to spend what remains on one useful explosion.

The Pale Dominion has no official position on Fragment Pulse. The spell destroys moon fragments — Yssara's living body — which is technically blasphemy. But the Dominion also fears Fracture Wyrms, and they have not objected to the Tide-Weavers' methods. The silence is pragmatic. Everyone pretends not to notice, and the fragments keep detonating, and the volunteers keep volunteering.

name: Memory Seal

relationships.label: The Greyvasti use Memory Seal to preserve their cultural history — elders seal their knowledge into moon fragments before death, creating an archive that survives the erosion of their minds.
The Tide-Weavers collect sealed memory fragments recovered from Greyvast's ruins — some of their most valuable 'discoveries' are Greyvasti memory archives sold without context or consent.
Memory Seal counters Vel-Thara's domain of forgetting — preserved memories resist her erosion, remaining intact and retrievable long after the original holder has been claimed by her silence.

description: Memory Seal is a spell that preserves a specific memory permanently outside the caster's mind by storing it in a moon fragment. The memory becomes retrievable by anyone who holds the fragment, but the caster loses it completely — it is gone, as if it never happened. The Greyvasti use this spell to preserve cultural memory before their elders die. The Tide-Weavers collect these sealed fragments and sell them as historical artifacts, often without the Greyvasti's blessing.
excerpt: Preserve a memory permanently in a moon fragment — the caster loses it, but anyone who holds the fragment can retrieve it. The Greyvasti use it to save their history.
content:
Memory Seal is not a difficult spell to cast. The difficulty is in the choice.

The caster holds a moon fragment — any grade, though the Greyvasti prefer small, pure pieces that can be worn as pendants or set into bracelets. They concentrate on the memory they wish to preserve. A face. A story. A song. The layout of a street that no longer exists. The spell transfers the memory from the caster's mind into the fragment's crystalline structure, where it settles into the glow like sediment in still water. The fragment becomes warm. The memory leaves the caster. It is not forgotten — it is simply not there anymore, as if it was never experienced.

The Greyvasti use this spell as a form of cultural preservation. An elder who feels the transformation beginning — the first flicker of silver in their eyes, the first gap in their recollection — will spend their remaining lucid days sealing memories into fragments. The family name. The location of Greyvast's original throne room. The recipe for mist-cured fish that only three people still know. Each seal is a small death, a piece of the elder erased and transferred to stone. When the elder finally Hollows, their memories remain in the fragments, retrievable by anyone who holds them.

The Tide-Weavers have discovered many of these sealed fragments in the ruins of Greyvast. They do not always return them to the Greyvasti. A sealed memory fragment from a pre-Fracture Greyvasti elder is worth more than a Grade 4 fragment on the open market — the sealed memories can be extracted, studied, and sold to scholars, collectors, and the Pale Dominion's scriptoriums. The Tide-Weavers argue that the fragments are salvage, legally recovered. The Greyvasti argue that their grandmother's last memory is not salvage. Both are correct, and the market decides.

Vel-Thara cannot touch memories preserved this way. Her domain is forgetting, loss, the slow erosion of everything that was. But a memory sealed in moon fragment is outside her reach — frozen in crystal, resistant to her influence. The Greyvasti do not worship Vel-Thara, but they understand her limitations. They seal their memories not despite her, but because of her. Every sealed fragment is a small act of defiance against the goddess who will eventually take everything else.
